newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says Arab countries owe it $1.4 billion.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says Arab countries owe it $1.4 billion.

text.p: Seven Arab countries owe Iraq $1.4 billion, Iraqi government newspapers said on Tuesday.
"The total amount of money due to be paid to Iraq by some Arab countries until the end of last September was $1,395,464,000," said the papers, quoting a source at the Iraqi Finance Ministry.
The papers named the countries as Saudi Arabia, Syria, Bahrain, Kuwait, Somalia, the United Arab Emirates and Egypt.
He said the money these states owed to Iraq covered loans offered by Iraq, oil exports, official bank deposits and profit of joint Arab companies.
Iraq's assets abroad, the bulk of them in U.S. and European banks, were impounded when it invaded Kuwait in 1990.

Baghdad has called many times for the release of its frozen assets in order to enable it buy food and medicine for its population, suffering from six-year-old trade sanctions for its invasion of Kuwait.
Imports of food and medicine are permitted under United Nations sanctions but blocking of oil export leaves Iraq short of funds to pay for them.

Iraq and the United Nations signed a deal in May which would allow Baghdad to export $2 billion worth of oil every six months to pay for urgently needed food and medicine. The pact was delayed last month after Iraqi military intervention in Kurdish in-fighting.
